question.text: Pushkar Growth Fund (Cat I-VCF) has received SEBI registration and declared first close at INR 85 crore. The investment team has identified a target Series-A deal and wants to make the first investment within 30 days of first close. Per SEBI Circular dated 12-Jan-2024 on custodian appointment, when must the custodian be appointed?

answer.text: Prior to the date of the first investment of the scheme
Only if the scheme reaches INR 500 crore corpus
At the time of fund winding up

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD/CIR/2024/5 dated 12-Jan-2024 ('Guidelines for AIFs with respect to holding their investments in dematerialized form and appointment of custodian') requires custodians for a scheme of an AIF to be appointed PRIOR to the date of first investment of the scheme. This tightens the earlier practice of post-investment custodian onboarding. **The Trap:** The 6-month-first-close option is wrong — it's linked to first investment, not first close. The INR 500 cr option cites the obsolete threshold (removed by 2024 amendment). The winding-up option is nonsensical. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers the same 2024 Circular. Older XIX-C / XIX-A papers pre-2024 may say 'on or before first investment' without the strict 'prior to' framing — use the current rule. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Budget 4-6 weeks of lead time for custodian onboarding: KYC, demat account opening, custodial agreement negotiation, settlement SLA setup. If your deal timeline is shorter, back-solve — accelerate custodian onboarding in parallel with PPM filing, NOT sequentially.
